title: New York City
summary: Manhattan, Canarsee, Hackensack and Rockaway peoples lived on the land before the Dutch colony of New Amsterdam began to form by 1624. It became seat of government of New Netherland in 1625, a major North Atlantic trading port by the 1650s, and passed to the British in 1664. It was national capital until 1790, and Washington took his presidential oath there in 1789.

as_recorded.value: 1625 Town of Nieuw Amsterdam becomes seat of government for Nieuw Netherlands.
1785 New York City becomes state capital (until 1789) and national capital (until 1790).

reviewer_note: Start year 1624 follows the NPS (colony 'began to be formed' by 1624); the city government dates the seat of government to 1625 and Lenape-area peoples to about 1000, so the span begins with the Dutch settlement, not earlier occupation. The 1626 Manhattan purchase is left out as its terms are contested. The sources opened do not state the renaming.
